text:
maya: quick heads-up — during the 02:30 sync we found 6 external guests still member of 'infra-admins' after the role-aliasing change.

alex: which change? role-aliasing in the RBAC refactor last week?

maya: yes. we switched from explicit role ids to aliases `infra.admin -> infra-admins` in apply-policy. some SCIM mappings were still using the old `role_id` attr.

scim-bot: scheduled sync job completed: job_id=sync-2026-03-15-02:30, processed=1234, added=4, removed=3, warnings=6

lia: paste the user object for one of the guests?

maya: sure

maya: ```json
{"id":"ext-usr-987","userName":"jane.external@example.com","externalId":"okta|12345","schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"groups":[{"value":"infra.admin","display":"Infra Admins"}]}
```

alex: aha — group value is `infra.admin` (old). our provisioner treats group.value as alias key now, doesn't map to `infra-admins` automatically.

sec-bot: alert created: [P1] scim-mapping-drift — potential privilege drift for external guests :eyes: 

devops: also seeing a handful of KMS decrypt DENY logs around the same time for `svc-key-prod`, then fallback to `redwood-fallback-sa` happened. Log excerpt:

devops: ```
[2026-03-15T02:29:51Z] KMS:Decrypt user=redwood-scim-provisioner key=svc-key-prod result=DENIED err="key policy condition failed"
[2026-03-15T02:29:52Z] Auth:AssumeRole principal=scim-provisioner fallback=redwood-fallback-sa granted=true
```

lia: that fallback path should NOT escalate to admin groups. looks like the fallback account has more privileges than intended.

maya: timeline: RBAC alias change deployed at 02:25, KMS key policy rotated at 02:28, sync job ran at 02:30. combination permitted some external users to remain in admin group because mapping check failed and fallback granted membership.

alex: immediate mitigation suggestions?

maya: 1) revoke membership for external guests from infra-admins (manual reconcile) — running `scim-client remove-member --group infra-admins --filter external:true`

maya: 2) rotate fallback service account keys and reduce privileges; disable automatic fallback until keys validated

alex: 3) add a check in the provisioner: if mapping attr missing OR KMS decrypt fails, don't auto-assign admin-level groups; mark for manual review

lia: 4) add reconciliation job that rejects legacy group identifiers (infra.admin) and alerts on any matches during dry-run

devops: I'll run an immediate cron reconcile in dry-run mode and post results.

scim-bot: reconcile dry-run: found 6 matches, would remove 6 memberships (details DM'd to @maya)

maya: done — removed the 6 memberships. filing incident follow-up with timeline and remediation steps.

alex: postmortem action items: update mapping docs, add unit test for alias mapping, add KMS policy change checklist, and add alert on any use of `redwood-fallback-sa` for SCIM activities.

lia: also add an e2e test: deploy alias change in staging, run sync, confirm no legacy group strings are accepted.

devops: I've disabled automatic fallback in auth layer for provisioner until we've validated key rotation.

maya: thanks — I'll open the follow-up doc and assign owners. tagging infra and identity teams to confirm corrective actions. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: incident P1 closed (mitigated) — follow-up required: owners=maya,alex,lia,devops

maya: will add a scheduled audit for next 7 days to ensure no regressions.
